rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act
rules.requirement: Landlords may not ask about or consider criminal history until after a conditional offer, and may never consider non-conviction, expunged, sealed, pardoned, vacated or juvenile records. After an offer, only listed serious convictions within set look-back periods may be considered, with an individualized assessment and written reasons if the offer is withdrawn.
rules.key_value: No criminal-record inquiry before conditional offer; look-back 6 yrs (1st degree), 4 yrs (2nd/3rd), 1 yr (4th); penalties $1,000/$5,000/$10,000
rules.quoted_span: A housing provider shall not make any oral or written inquiry regarding an applicant’s criminal record prior to making a conditional offer
rules.effective_date_note: Approved June 18, 2021; takes effect first day of the seventh month next following enactment = 2022-01-01.
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental dwelling units offered by housing providers.
rules.exemptions: Dwelling units in owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.
rules.penalty: Up to $1,000 first violation; up to $5,000 with one prior in 5 years; up to $10,000 with two or more priors in 7 years. Enforced by Division on Civil Rights; no private court action; may require return of application fee.

unverifiable_exemptions: owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units

rules.title: NJ Law Against Discrimination: source of lawful income (incl. Section 8 vouchers)
rules.requirement: A landlord cannot refuse to rent to someone because of the lawful source of their income or rent payment, for example a Section 8 voucher. Complaints may be filed with the Division on Civil Rights within 180 days or in Superior Court within two years.
rules.key_value: ban on source-of-income (incl. Section 8 voucher) discrimination
rules.quoted_span: This means, for example, that a landlord cannot deny the lawful recipient of a Section 8 HUD voucher the right to rent an apartment based solely on that source of lawful income
rules.effective_date_note: Documents do not state when source-of-income protection took effect.
rules.exemptions: Rental of one apartment in an owner-occupied two-family dwelling; rooms in an owner-occupied one-family dwelling; religious organization preference.
rules.penalty: Up to $10,000 for a first offense (N.J.S.A. 10:5-14.1a).

unverifiable_exemptions: single apartment in owner-occupied two-family dwelling

rules.title: Residential rental application fee cap ($50, CPI-adjusted)
rules.requirement: A landlord or agent cannot charge more than $50 for an application or similar fee to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental. The cap is adjusted annually for CPI, and violators face penalties, with the wrongly charged amount remitted to the applicant.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord, or agent thereof, shall not require an application or other similar fee to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental property for dwelling purposes, which exceeds $50
rules.effective_date_note: Approved 2026-01-20; takes effect first day of the fourth month next following enactment = 2026-05-01.
rules.exemptions: Dwelling units in one- or two-family dwellings; NJ Real Estate Commission licensees unless the licensee is the landlord.
rules.penalty: Up to $500 first offense, $750 second, $1,000 each subsequent.

rules.title: NJ Security Deposit Law: cap, trust/interest handling and return
rules.requirement: A landlord may not collect a security deposit above 1.5 times one month's rent (annual increases max 10%), and prepaid rent counts toward the cap; with first month's rent, no more than 2.5 months at lease start. Deposits are held in trust in an interest-bearing NJ account with written notice within 30 days, and must be returned with interest less itemized deductions within 30 days after tenancy ends, or the tenant may sue for double.
rules.key_value: 1.5 months' rent max; return within 30 days; double damages if wrongfully withheld
rules.quoted_span: The maximum-security deposit to be collected by the landlord cannot be more than one and one-half times one month’s rent
rules.effective_date_note: Document does not state an effective date.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings (tenant may opt in by written request, effective 30 days later); seasonal rentals (125 days or less) exempt from the interest-bearing account section.
rules.penalty: Double the amount wrongly withheld plus costs and attorney's fees; tenant may apply deposit plus 7% interest to rent if notice/interest not provided; $500-$2,000 civil penalty for willful withholding from assisted tenants.

unverifiable_exemptions: owner-occupied two- or three-family dwelling (tenant may opt in)

rules.title: NJ Anti-Eviction Act (good cause, notices to quit, grounds, owner-occupied rules)
rules.requirement: A landlord may remove a tenant only through court process and must have a statutory good cause (e.g., nonpayment, disorderly conduct, lease breach, conversion, owner occupancy); a lease cannot be non-renewed just because the term ended. Except for nonpayment, a written Notice to Quit (sometimes preceded by a Notice to Cease) is required, with periods from 3 days to 3 years depending on the ground; lockouts are illegal, and rent-increase evictions need a notice to quit and notice of increase. Misusing owner-occupancy or removal notices can bring treble damages and civil penalties up to $10,000.
rules.key_value: Good cause required; Notice to Quit 3 days to 3 years depending on ground
rules.quoted_span: No residential landlord may evict or fail to renew a lease, whether it is a written or an oral lease without good cause
rules.effective_date_note: Document does not state an effective date.
rules.coverage_conditions: Most residential rentals including single-family homes, mobile homes, apartment buildings, rooming and boarding houses.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings have separate, narrower rules (2A:18-61.2); hotel/motel transient or seasonal guests; units held in trust for a developmentally disabled family member.
rules.penalty: Treble damages plus fees and civil penalty up to $10,000 for misuse of occupancy/removal notices (2A:18-61.6); damages for self-help eviction.

unverifiable_exemptions: unit held in trust for developmentally disabled family member

rules.review_note: Foreclosure notice and senior/disabled conversion protections described in the same guide are related but separate laws and were not given their own records.

rules.title: NJ tenant reprisal (retaliation) protection
rules.requirement: A landlord cannot evict, substantially change lease terms, or refuse to renew in retaliation for a tenant enforcing rights, making good-faith health or safety complaints, or joining a tenant organization. The tenant may sue for damages.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord cannot take reprisal action against a tenant by eviction, substantial alteration of a lease or its terms, or refusal to renew a lease when a tenant exercises certain civil rights

rules.title: Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act
rules.requirement: Landlords may not pay for or use a coordinator's algorithmic rent-pricing software or device that pools nonpublic competitor data or sets parallel pricing, and no one may perform such a coordinating function or facilitate parallel pricing coordination. Violations are violations of the NJ Antitrust Act, and municipalities may not enact conflicting ordinances.
rules.key_value: ban on algorithmic coordinators / parallel pricing coordination in residential rentals
rules.quoted_span: a rental property owner, or any agent, representative, or subcontractor thereof, to receive, subscribe to, contract for, or otherwise exchange any form of consideration in return for the use of, the services of a coordinator;
rules.effective_date_note: First day of the twelfth month next following enactment (approved 2026-07-20) = 2027-07-01; matches Day Pitney alert.
rules.coverage_conditions: Any rental residential dwelling unit in the State.
rules.exemptions: Research/statistical use, free public rent estimates, equal-terms brokerage databases, government affordability controls; inpatient medical, long-term care, detention facilities.
rules.penalty: Violation of the New Jersey Antitrust Act; sections 6-17 enforcement applies; AG complaint portal.
rules.interaction: Section 6(b) bars municipal ordinances that conflict with the act.
rules.conflict_note: May preempt conflicting local ordinances (Jersey City § 218-12, Hoboken ch. 158, Art. II) from 2027-07-01; flag for human review.

unverifiable_exemptions: inpatient medical care, licensed long-term care, detention facilities

no_rule_findings.finding: New Jersey has no statewide rent control or cap on rent increases; municipalities may adopt rent control or leveling ordinances. Increases need proper notice and must not be unconscionable. Newly constructed multiple dwellings are exempt from local rent control for 30 years after construction (N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.5), which limits local ordinances.
no_rule_findings.quoted_span: The State of New Jersey has no laws that establish, govern or control rents.

parsed.notes: Merged deposit and Anti-Eviction Act candidates into single records. The 30-year new-construction exemption (c53) is not a separate rule; it belongs in the coverage of local rent control ordinances (new_construction_exemption 30 years, construction_completed). Foreclosure and senior conversion protections dropped as secondary laws. No link-only additions made.
